### Part 1: Learn the game

#### The Very Basics

##### A Brief History of Chess

I'm not a historian. \

\

I consider chess to be one of the first transmissions of pop culture through the medieval world. In the carts of the same caravans that carried silks and spices, came a less commodified good. It was a game. It was a game played by kings and nobility, perhaps the only class with the disposable income and time for a game back then. As such, it appealed to it's target audience, depicting epic battles, with flanking and central thrusts, demonstrating the value of a strong tactic, and often having the valiant kings duke it out for positioning after most of the expendables had laid their life's out already. \

\

The name for chess also progressed from the old world to the new, in an evolution that resembled a game of broken telephone. Originally called chaturanga or the four armed God, the name would drop syllables and change letters through the centuries. \

\

The Persians called it Shatrung.\

\

The Spanish, ejedrez, which turned into the French echecs (which gives us the modern chess term of check' in English) Finally (for our purposes at least) the game would become chess in English around the year blank. \

\

From there, the colonial empire of Queen Victoria took the game to the rest of the world not accessible by horseback or 12th century gallon. \

\

The next point of importance for us is the proliferation of the modern, professional game circuit. This is when we begin to have a real supply of historical games to work with. There are exceptions from the medieval era such as blank. \

\

The World Chess championship started in blank. \

\

Today's reigning champion is Magnus Carlsen. \

\

I won't touch on the growing impact computers have had on chess yet, we'll get back to that. \

##### Knowing Where You Come From

Taking on a new endeavour comes with an appetite to succeed. This is a good instinct, and quite possibly the reason you're turning to this book for advice.\
\
We're all inextricably tied to what's come before us. This isn't something that comes packaged with the information we consume either. \
When you read a headline, there's likely historical context that's missing. A new fad comes into on a wave that washes out what just came before it. \
\
Stepping back in a temporal sense can help you get a sense of the larger machinations at play, and bring peace in knowing your problems aren't new, they've been addressed many times before. Learn from the masters. \
\
I'm the only child of 1st generation Indian immigrants to Canada. By in large, I behave more Canadian than I do Indian. For me Canada was everything there ever had been. It took me going back to my ancestral home in India to understand what's at stake for me to succeed. \
\
On the way back to my hometown, I saw destitute poverty like never before. I will one day inherit a modest home in the Indian farmlands, along with an acre of arable land. This is not something my father bought before moving. My family had been farmers for 1000s of years before me. I was the first in my family to go to university, to travel to more than 2 countries, and to fall in love with someone who wasn't Punjabi. \
\
I also came to appreciate that the lavished of the western world had been built to some extent on the backs of cheap labour and raw materials from places my mine. \
\
Learning and appreciating our past in terms of family, history and culture, helps us better position our current goals and aspirations within context. \

##### The Setup

Chess is a game played with a board and pieces. The board is covered by 64 identical squares, their only variance being that they are coloured black and white in an alternating manner. When setting up a chess board, there should be a white square on the bottom right corner from both player's perspectives. Remember "white on the right." I had a few embarassing games early on where things didn't quite look right until I spotted this mistake.\
\
There are 34 pieces. They are coloured either dark or light, which each player getting a set placed on their side of the board. The pieces begin in the same squares at the start of each game. Only one piece can occupy a square at any given time. \
\
Here are drawings of how each piece commonly looks:\
\
Here is how the pieces should be placed on the board at the start of each game.\
\
The only pieces that aren't placed symmetrically are the queen and king. Remember that a player must place their queen piece on the same colour as their piece colour. If you have the light pieces, your queen must be on the rear central light square. Remember: Queen on her colour\
\
The objective of a game of chess is to put the opponents king piece into a position known as checkmate.

#### Why Chess?

\*\*myfile 
\

\
Believe it or not, chess was a pursuit that intimidated me in my younger years. \
\
Grade 5 Chess Club\
- Rockey travelling to other schools\
- Crying after losing a game\
\
- Picked it up again in my mid-20s\
- Began to like the game\
- Learned to dig beyond the rules and get to the strategy\
- Get beyond the rules - 1
st
 lesson.\
\
What it taught me:\
\
Chess is dying. So it critical thinking and informed decision making. Here's how we go about saving both;\
\
Chess is not about instant gratification. Chess, when played properly, is about concentration, mesuring twice and cutting once. Chess often ends in a draw. Going for brought, while fun is not what makes you a good chess player, or a good decision maker in life.\
\
At this amateur level, I will say: don't be so afraid of losing ground, that you avoid taking calculated risks. If you sacrifice a piece, have 2 good follow-up moves, but don't be so concerned about making sure the sequence leaves you in an absolutely winning position. If you're mathematically losing, don't turn in the towel immediately, and also don't play snail-like, aggravating your opponent to no end until they eventually win 100 moves later. Play romantic. Sacrifice even more material to open up lines. Keep things exciting.\
\
This won't make you a great player past the advanced amateur stage, but it will make sure you have fun, while most improtantly, not stopping you from learning.
